verdict.headline: Inflation expectations jumped and a September hike became near-certain, but stocks rallied
verdict.label: Core CPI rose 0.3% against a 0.2% estimate with shelter at 0.3%, preliminary September consumer sentiment fell to 47.8 with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.6% from 4.0%, and September 16 hike odds moved to roughly 90% from about 71%; the S&P 500 still rose 0.86% to 7,656.98 as WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.4%
verdict.rationale_short:
August headline CPI was in line and the annual core rate slowed to 2.4% from 2.5%, but the monthly core rose 0.3% against a 0.2% estimate, up from 0.2% in July, with the shelter index accelerating to 0.3% after two consecutive months at 0.1%. Shelter is roughly a third of the index and cannot be attributed to the Strait of Hormuz, which is why an in-line headline moved rate pricing at all.

Ninety minutes after the open the University of Michigan put preliminary September sentiment at 47.8 against a 51.0 estimate, down 7.5% and the second-lowest reading in a series that starts in 1952, with the expectations component down 15.7% to 45.8. Year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.6% from 4.0% and the long-run measure to 3.4%. Futures finished pricing roughly a 90% probability of a quarter-point increase on September 16, from about 71% before the data. Anchored expectations are the stated reason a central bank can look through an energy shock, and the year-ahead series moved six tenths in a month, four days before a decision, with the committee in blackout through September 17 and unable to frame the number either way.

Equities rose through all of it. The S&P 500 gained 0.86% to 7,656.98, its first advance in five sessions, the Dow 0.98% and the Nasdaq 0.96%, while the VIX fell 10.79% to 15.92. The rally was bought on crude coming off its high — WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.4%, after Iranian state media said Tehran will meet Gulf states in Oman to discuss the Strait of Hormuz — and on AI capital spending news, with Dell up about 12% to a record and Oracle up about 7.5%.

The evidence cuts both ways and the divergence should not be read as one side being wrong. Stocks priced a decelerating input; the rate market priced what that input has already done to expectations. Both readings are internally consistent, and the split shows inside the equity market itself: the Russell 2000 rose 0.4% against the Dow's 0.98%, so the rate-sensitive part of the market declined to endorse the rally. The relief in crude is also narrower than it looks — WTI held the $100 settle this week's rate repricing was built on, by five cents, on the week's clearest de-escalation headline, and still ended the week up 9.4%. The ten-year finished at 4.96%, its highest close of this cycle, on a day crude fell, which separates the rates move from the energy shock that started it.

What would change the picture: the final September sentiment reading on September 25 holding at or above 4.6% makes the expectations move structural, while a revision back toward 4.2% makes it an energy artifact. A WTI settle under $100 takes the input out of the October data the September decision will never see; a return above $104 puts a second month of pass-through into the November meeting's data. On the curve, a ten-year close through 5.00% before Wednesday would say the market expects a hike that does not settle the inflation question; a retreat under 4.90% on a delivered hike would say it does. The thirty-year at roughly 5.36% has the 2007 peak of 5.44% above it.
verdict.lede_short: Core inflation ran a tenth hot on shelter, and consumers' year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.6% from 4.0% with sentiment at its second-lowest reading on record — taking September 16 hike odds to roughly 90% from 71%. Stocks rallied anyway, the S&P 500 up 0.86%, bought on crude easing to a $100.05 settle. Equities priced a decelerating input; the bond market priced what it already did to expectations.

supporting_data.label: Preliminary September consumer sentiment fell 7.5% to 47.8 against a 51.0 estimate, the second-lowest reading since 1952, with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.6% from 4.0% and the long-run measure at 3.4% — anchored expectations are the stated reason a central bank can look through an energy shock, and this series moved six tenths in a month

Core CPI rose 0.3% in August, one tenth above most estimates and up from 0.2% in July, with shelter at 0.3% after two months at 0.1%, while core over twelve months slowed to 2.4% from 2.5% — the annual rate decelerated on base effects while the monthly rate accelerated in the largest non-energy component, which is the part the bond market traded

Futures finished pricing roughly a 90% probability of a quarter-point increase on September 16, up from about 71% before the data — a nineteen-point move in one session on a print whose headline was in line places the repricing in the core and expectations lines rather than the aggregate

WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.4%, and Brent at $104.61, down 2.8%, after Iranian state media said Tehran will meet Gulf states in Oman over the Strait of Hormuz, leaving WTI up 9.4% on the week — the $100 settle this week's rate repricing was built on held by five cents, so the relief equities bought is a decelerating input rather than a departing one

The ten-year yield finished at 4.96%, its highest close of this cycle, and the two-year at 4.63% — the curve rose on the day crude fell, which separates the rates move from the energy shock that started it

The S&P 500 rose 65.28 points to 7,656.98 and the Dow 509.19 points to 52,573.29, but the Russell 2000 added only 0.4% to 2,903.94 — the rate-sensitive part of the equity market gained a fifth of what the Dow did, declining to endorse the rally

watchlist_mentions.note: WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.4%, on the announcement that Tehran will meet Gulf states in Oman over Hormuz. The level this week's rate repricing was built on held by five cents on the week's clearest de-escalation headline, and crude still ended the week up 9.4%.

Rose about 12% to a record $566.99 after RBC initiated at Outperform with a $640 target, extending a roughly 350% run this year. The July quarter carried $60.9 billion of AI-related orders and a $95 billion backlog, with FY27 revenue guidance lifted to a $192 billion midpoint from $167 billion.

Gained about 7.5%, recovering Thursday's 5.38% decline, on cloud infrastructure revenue up 121% to $7.4 billion and remaining performance obligations of $664 billion. The two-session round trip leaves the stock near where it started the week; $28.5 billion of quarterly capital spending against negative $5.4 billion of free cash flow is the unchanged constraint.

Added about 1.3%, a partial recovery from Thursday's 2.4% decline on the Justice Department review of the $20 billion Groq licensing structure. The inquiry has produced a formal request for information and no filed action, so the move is positioning rather than news.

December futures settled at $4,408.90, up $1.60, essentially flat on a day hike odds moved to roughly 90%. Last night's report named a hold above $4,400 into the CPI print as the sign that haven demand was still underneath the real-rate selling; it held.

Near $77,000 in a tenth consecutive session below $80,000. It took no bid from either the equity rally or the crude pullback, and continues to trade with the rate-sensitive assets rather than as a haven.

trade_setups.asset: Consumer inflation expectations at 4.6% into the final September reading
trade_setups.thesis: The preliminary year-ahead figure jumped six tenths to 4.6% and the long-run measure ticked to 3.4%, on a survey period dominated by $100 crude and record retail diesel. Anchored expectations are the stated basis on which a committee can look through an energy shock, so this is the series that decides whether the September hike is a one-off response to oil or the start of a sequence. Revisions to the preliminary reading have been large in both directions this year.
trade_setups.entry: 4.6% on the year-ahead measure and 3.4% on the long-run are the levels; the final September reading on September 25 is the confirmation.
trade_setups.invalidation: A final reading revised back toward 4.2% would make the move an energy artifact the committee can discount at its November meeting.
trade_setups.horizon: September 25, then into the November decision

trade_setups.thesis: Crude fell 2.4% on the announcement of Iran-Gulf talks in Oman over the Strait of Hormuz and still settled above $100, ending the week up 9.4%. The distinction the morning report drew between an intraday print and a settle held: the week's clearest de-escalation headline did not break the level. US retail diesel remains at a record with distillate stockpiles at their lowest on record for the time of year, and refiners reached 52-week highs on the day crude fell, which is product margin widening as the input cheapens.
trade_setups.entry: $100 on the settle is the level, and the Iran-Oman transit route is the catalyst; it carries no fixed date.
trade_setups.invalidation: A settle under $100 takes the energy input out of the October data the September decision will never see; a return above $104 puts a second month of pass-through into the November meeting's data.
trade_setups.horizon: Next week's settles, into the transit-route window

trade_setups.asset: The ten-year at 4.96% into the September 16 decision
trade_setups.thesis: The ten-year closed at its highest of this cycle on a day crude fell 2.4% and equity volatility dropped 10.79%, which locates the move in the policy path rather than in the oil premium. August retail sales at 8:30 a.m. on decision day, with consensus at 0.2% against 0.5% in July, puts a growth reading hours ahead of a hike aimed at an energy shock the Fed cannot supply.
trade_setups.entry: 5.00% is the level above 4.96%; the thirty-year at roughly 5.36% has the 2007 peak of 5.44% above it.
trade_setups.invalidation: A retreat under 4.90% on a delivered hike would say the market reads the increase as settling the inflation question rather than opening a sequence.
trade_setups.horizon: Through the September 16 decision and the September 17 end of blackout
